title: FTC Settlement Over 'Active Listening' AI Marketing Claims
description: The FTC required Cox Media Group and two other firms to pay nearly $1 million for deceiving customers about 'Active Listening' AI-powered marketing. The service didn't actually listen to conversations but resold email lists from data brokers at a markup. Simon Willison's previous analysis that this was just a metaphor for standard ad targeting was confirmed.
author: Simon Willison

title: 5 Best AI Coding Agents in 2026: Claude Code vs Cursor vs Copilot
description: Comprehensive comparison of top AI coding agents in 2026, evaluating Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and other leading tools in terms of capabilities, performance, and developer experience.
author: Fungies

title: MOSS: Self-Evolution through Source-Level Rewriting in Autonomous Agent Systems
description: ArXiv paper introducing MOSS, a system for autonomous agent self-evolution through source-level rewriting. Presents a framework where agents can modify their own code to improve capabilities over time.
author: Qianshu Cai, Yonggang Zhang, et al.

title: Claw AI Lab: An Autonomous Multi-Agent Research Team
description: ArXiv paper presenting Claw AI Lab, an autonomous multi-agent research team that can conduct research collaboratively. The system demonstrates how multiple AI agents can work together on complex research tasks.
author: Fan Wu, Cheng Chen, et al.

title: Compiling Agentic Workflows into LLM Weights
description: ArXiv paper proposing a method to compile agentic workflows directly into LLM weights, achieving near-frontier quality at two orders of magnitude less cost. Represents a significant advance in making AI agents more efficient.
author: Simon Dennis, Rivaan Patil, et al.

title: TerminalWorld: Benchmarking Agents on Real-World Terminal Tasks
description: ArXiv paper introducing TerminalWorld, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on real-world terminal tasks. Provides a standardized way to measure agent performance on practical command-line operations.
author: Zhaoyang Chu, Jiarui Hu, et al.

title: WorkstreamBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on End-to-End Spreadsheet Tasks in Finance
description: ArXiv paper presenting WorkstreamBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on realistic end-to-end spreadsheet tasks in finance. Focuses on practical business applications of AI agents.
author: Thomson Yen, Julian Poeltl, et al.

title: Datasette Agent: Extensible AI Assistant for Datasette
description: Simon Willison announced the first release of Datasette Agent, a new extensible AI assistant for Datasette that represents the integration of his LLM Python library (3+ years in development) with Datasette. The tool includes per-user spending limits, SQL execution permissions, and Fly Sprites sandbox command execution.
author: Simon Willison

title: SpaceX-Anthropic $1.25B/Month Compute Agreement
description: SpaceX S-1 filing revealed Cloud Services Agreements with Anthropic for access to compute capacity across COLOSSUS and COLOSSUS II. Anthropic agreed to pay $1.25 billion per month through May 2029, with capacity ramping in May-June 2026 at reduced fees. 90-day termination notice allowed.
author: Simon Willison

title: Andrej Karpathy: Programming Has Fundamentally Changed in Last 2 Months
description: Karpathy tweeted about a dramatic shift in programming due to AI, stating it's 'hard to communicate how much programming has changed due to AI in the last 2 months.' He revealed that AI agents now write 80% of his code and he hasn't written a line of code in months, noting coding agents basically didn't work before December and now basically work.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: Gemini 3.5 Flash Release and Antigravity CLI Transition
description: Google released Gemini 3.5 Flash at Google I/O, using it across key products. Announced Gemini Spark as an OpenClaw competitor, and revealed transition from open-source Gemini CLI (TypeScript, Apache 2.0) to closed-source Antigravity CLI (Go-based) starting June 18th. Security approach includes isolated VMs and Agent Gateway with DLP policies.
author: Simon Willison

title: The Last Six Months in LLMs - PyCon US Lightning Talk
description: Simon Willison delivered a five-minute lightning talk at PyCon US 2026 summarizing the last six months of LLM developments. Used his annotated presentation tool to create slides covering key recent advances in AI and language models.
author: Simon Willison

title: From Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering
description: At Sequoia AI Ascent 2026, Karpathy discussed the evolution from 'vibe coding' (coined last year) to 'agentic engineering.' He explained: 'vibe coding raised the floor. Agentic engineering raises the ceiling' - representing a shift in how developers build seriously with AI agents.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: UK Government Digital Service Backs Open Source for AI Code
description: Government Digital Service (GDS) published 'AI, open code and vulnerability risk in the public sector' recommending keeping open by default. This is seen as a major escalation in response to NHS closing open source repos after Project Glasshook vulnerabilities. Making everything private adds delivery costs and reduces scrutiny.
author: Simon Willison (covering Terence Eden)

title: OpenClaw's Name Evolution: Warelay to OpenClaw
description: Analysis of OpenClaw's six-month name evolution since November 2025: Warelay → CLAWDIS → CLAWDBOT → Clawdbot → Moltbot → OpenClaw. Shows rapid iteration on AI assistant product identity and positioning.
author: Simon Willison
